Financial implications of the risk or opportunity (Indicate positive or negative implications)

i) Physical risks can affect macroeconomic stability and inflation dynamics, impacting real interest rates. Transition risks arising from a country’s climate exposure, energy mix and policy response may affect the fiscal position and sovereign credit profile. ii) Physical risks (extreme weather events) and transition risks (policy, technology and market shifts affecting carbon- intensive issuers) can increase financial stress on investee entities and affect their repayment capacity. iii) Physical risks such as extreme weather events, rising sea levels and flooding can cause damage to assets, particularly in high-risk locations. Transition risks may render existing assets less efficient or redundant. iv) Physical risks (heat, flooding, storms) can disrupt IT infrastructure. Transition risks may arise from the need to shift to more energy-efficient systems. The growing market for green, sovereign green and sustainability-linked bonds offers avenues for portfolio diversification aligned with the Company’s core dealing expertise, and positions the Company to participate in the evolving sustainable finance ecosystem.

i Conduct regular risk assessments, assessing portfolio and account level exposure, and develop risk management plans and infrastructure resilience. ii Positive screening for green and sustainable instruments (subject to risk- reward analysis) and building of capability in the green and ESG- labelled fixed- income segment.

Positive: New revenue streams, portfolio diversification and enhanced market positioning. Negative: i) Potential adverse impact on interest rates and market valuation of the investment portfolio. ii) Write-offs, higher repair & maintenance costs, and early retirement of assets. iii) Potential operational disruption and additional capital expenditure on upgradation.

5. Specific commitments, goals and targets set by the entity with defined timelines, if any.

The Company aims to move towards carbon neutrality by FY 2031. Towards this objective, it intends to progressively reduce its emissions through a combination of measures such as transition towards cleaner vehicle options, improvement in energy efficiency, greater use of green energy sources, and other operational initiatives. Residual emissions, where required, are proposed to be addressed through suitable offset mechanisms. The Carbon neutrality Plan provides framework for gradual reduction of exposure in carbon-intensive sectors in non-Government Securities portfolio, along with a measured increase in investment in green and sustainable bonds, subject to risk- return considerations. In addition, adoption of energy-efficient equipment and CSR activities focused on environmental sustainability are other operational measures defined for achieving carbon neutrality by 2031. These measures will be reviewed periodically by an Internal Committee, under the oversight of the Risk Management Committee and the Board.

The Company remains committed to integrating sustainability considerations into its governance framework, business strategy and operations while periodically reviewing progress towards its environmental, social and governance (ESG) objectives. As the defined commitments are long-term in nature with milestones extending up to FY 2031 and beyond, no interim targets were due during the reporting period. Accordingly, no deviations from the approved commitments have been observed, and progress will continue to be monitored and reported periodically through the established governance mechanism.

9. Does the entity have a specified Committee of the Board/ Director responsible for decision making on sustainability related issues? (Yes / No). If yes, provide detail.

Yes. The Company has established a governance framework for overseeing sustainability-related matters. An internal BRSR Committee, comprising the Managing Director & CEO, Company Secretary (designated as the BRSR Head), and Functional Heads – SEVP/CXOs are responsible for coordinating, monitoring, and reporting sustainability-related disclosures in accordance with the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) framework. At the Board level, the Risk Management Committee (RMC) has been entrusted with the responsibility of overseeing, monitoring, and reviewing sustainability and climate-related risks and opportunities. The Committee periodically assesses the potential impact of such risks on the Company’s business and provides recommendations to the Board. The Board of Directors retains overall responsibility for sustainability-related matters and approves significant sustainability-related policies, strategies, and initiatives based on the recommendations and inputs of the Risk Management Committee and the management team.

The Company undertakes Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and its CSR Policy, with a focus on creating meaningful social and environmental impact. The selection of CSR projects is based on identified community needs, alignment with the Company’s CSR objectives, and the expertise of implementing partners. During the reporting period, while the Company implemented various CSR initiatives across different geographies, none of the projects were specifically located in districts designated as Aspirational Districts by the Government of India. Nevertheless, the Company remains committed to supporting inclusive and sustainable development and will continue to explore opportunities for undertaking impactful interventions in underserved and priority regions, including Aspirational Districts, where feasible and aligned with its CSR strategy.
